name.description: The name shown in the project's media list, usually the file name.

ApiError.description: The body of every error response.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable identifier such as `unauthorized`.

CanPlayAnswer.description: A media element's `canPlayType` answer. The empty string becomes `No`.

bit_rate.description: The overall bit rate of the file in bits per second.

budget_bytes.description: The size the cache may grow to when disk space allows.

limit_bytes.description: The size the cache may currently grow to: the budget, reduced when free space is short.

space_low.description: True when free disk space, not the budget, limits the cache.

ConversionReason.description: Why the file is converted rather than played directly.

Cue.description:
One text segment with the time range during which it is shown.

The text keeps any inline markup from the source file, such as `<i>`, and joins
multiple lines with `\n`.

MediaFile.description: A video or audio file added to a project.

name.description: The name shown in the project's media list, usually the file name.

track_selection_json.description:
The user's saved choice of video and audio tracks, as the JSON the media crate
defines. Null until the user has chosen.

last_modified_ms.description: The file's modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

MediaFileSource.description:
Where the bytes of a media file come from.

The `path` variant names a file on the machine running the server. The `browser_file`
variant describes a file the web app holds in memory; the server never sees its bytes,
so it records only what identifies the file when the user picks it again.

ParseTimedTextRequest.description: The request body shared by the HTTP route and the WebAssembly facade.

PlaybackEngine.description: The browser engine behind the media element, decided from the user agent.

can_play_type.description: The answer to `canPlayType` for the file's direct MIME type with codecs.

mse_codec_strings.description: The RFC 6381 codec strings that `MediaSource.isTypeSupported` accepts in fragmented MP4.

oneOf.description: The client plays the file's own bytes in a media element.

allOf.description: The server converts the file into HLS with fragmented MP4 segments while it plays.

oneOf.description: The server converts the file into HLS with fragmented MP4 segments while it plays.
The user's preferred converted audio codec; the server's default when absent.
The tracks to play; the default selection when absent.

playlist_path.description: The path of the HLS playlist, present only when the plan converts.

PreferenceValue.description: A preference value. `null` means the preference has not been set.

Rational.description: A positive ratio of two integers, such as a timebase of `1/90000` or a frame rate of `30000/1001`.

TextSource.description:
Where the text of a request comes from.

The `path` variant names a file on the machine running the server. The server resolves
it, and only for requests authenticated with the per-launch token. The WebAssembly build
supports only the `inline` variant.

TrackInfo.description: One stream inside a container. Fields the source does not state are `None`.

codec.description: ffmpeg's name for the codec, such as `h264`, `aac`, or `subrip`.

codec_string.description:
The RFC 6381 codec string in the spelling Media Source Extensions accept,
or `None` when the codec cannot be carried in fragmented MP4.

container_track_id.description:
The identifier the container itself uses for the track, such as the MP4 track id
or the Matroska track number, when known.

index.description: The stream's position counted over all stream kinds, as in ffmpeg's `0:N`.

language.description: The language tag stored in the container, or `None` when it is undetermined.

profile.description: ffmpeg's name for the codec profile, such as `High` or `LC`.

direct_mime_type.description:
The MIME type with codecs to pass to `canPlayType`, or `None` when the file's own bytes
cannot play in a media element at all.

oneOf.description: Transcode to H.264, scaled to `scale_to` when set, at `bit_rate` bits per second.

WaveformResponse.description:
One window of waveform peaks: 100 per second from `start_ms`, each the loudest sample of the
loudest channel in its hundredth of a second, from 0 (silence) to 255 (full scale).
